Recommended design: predeclare three GRU4Rec conditions—unchanged baseline; full-context training with exactly the cropped condition’s supervised target positions, negatives, loss weights and normalization; cropped-context training. The cropped-versus-matched-control contrast estimates the effect of context removal; matched-control-versus-baseline reveals effects of altered supervision. Keep initialization, optimizer, update count and inference fixed. Derive separate reproducible random streams from seed 42 for user/negative sampling, cropping and dropout, so crop draws cannot perturb sampling or dropout. Align corresponding draws across conditions where possible; identical seeds alone do not guarantee alignment when execution changes. This applies the variance-reduction principle of [common random numbers](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.38.6.884).

For uncertainty, retain each validation user’s binary hit outcome on identical pinned candidates. Compute paired differences, resample users within each category using identical indices across conditions, then average the four category differences equally; report a paired 95% bootstrap interval and category-level gains/losses. [SciPy documents this paired resampling](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html). With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the trained models and candidates; one training seed cannot establish robustness across training randomness. Predeclare crop settings, checkpoint rules and contrasts, cap validation queries, and record every attempted configuration: repeatedly selecting validation winners creates optimism that ordinary bootstrap intervals do not remove ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Preserve the host’s 99-negative protocol, but limit conclusions to that sampled benchmark; sampled rankings can disagree with full-catalog evaluation ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).
